arithmetic.note: the checkerboard is the unique arrangement that saturates both cell types: rich cannot hold a third, poor cannot hold a second

fires.evidence: n=42 (two seats too many) must fall back to 60, not stay above it: alive = 42, overfull cells = []

silent.evidence: n=40 must reproduce EXP-66: alive = 40, moving = 0

specific.evidence: n=39: empty cells = [39] (rich [], poor [39]); on_max+on_min = 39 vs alive = 39. The hole must be POOR: a hole at a rich cell fills, because a neighbour on a poor cell sees a richer neighbour and walks onto it.

verdict.reason: hole kept = [39] (empty [39]), excess died = False (alive 42 at n=42). At least one push rearranged the arrangement, so it is a reachable state and not an attractor.

limitations: The pushes are a missing seat and extra seats. Neither is a local rearrangement at fixed count -- moving one organism from a rich cell to a poor cell while every other organism stays put. The trace binary cannot express that start, so 'stable' here does not yet mean 'stable against every rearrangement'.

Only one field amplitude is tested (rich 2.4 / poor 1.6). A weaker contrast may have a different arrangement, and the arithmetic above says when: the poor cell stops feeding one when min(M_poor, income) < need, i.e. below M_poor = 0.675.
move_cost is 0, so this says nothing about whether moving is affordable -- only about where the population ends up when it is free.
